segments: This article is adapted from shorinkiwata/archlinuxinstall, preserving the original tutorial's operational detail while anonymizing it and correcting risk-related guidance. Package names, extensions, drivers, and interfaces may change with rolling updates. All commands below are examples for reading and were neither executed nor verified during this task.

This article follows the UEFI + Btrfs + GRUB installation path. Back up your data first, verify the disk and partitions, and distinguish a new ESP from an existing dual-boot ESP. Writing a partition table with cfdisk or formatting with mkfs.* can delete data. Run these operations only on targets explicitly approved for recreation, and do not format Windows' existing ESP. Every /dev/*_partition or /dev/EXAMPLE_DISK must be replaced with a target verified on the actual machine; these are not device names ready to run as written.

The swapfile size 4g is only an example. Hibernation requires the target swap space to hold the actual hibernation image, with the resume location configured correctly. A Btrfs subvolume containing an active swapfile cannot have ordinary snapshots taken; a separate @swap helps isolate this restriction.
References: A Concise Guide to Arch Linux Installation Guide - Arch Linux Chinese Wiki

For a new ESP, start by planning for 1 GiB with the EFI System type; allocate the remaining space as Linux filesystem partitions as needed. If an ESP already exists for dual boot, inspect it first and do not recreate or format it.
Check mount points and partition numbers: formatting deletes the partition's data. Mount an existing dual-boot ESP without formatting it.
Write a hostname of your choice into /etc/hostname, for example workstation, to avoid embedding a personal device name in public configuration.

Run archinstall to Start the Installation Script (Use the Arrow Keys to Move, Enter to Select, Tab to Toggle Checkboxes, and / to Search)

For mirror, select your region or country, or leave the selection automatic. Enable the 32-bit repository (multilib) under optional repositories: gaming or running Windows programs requires 32-bit support.
The wiki recommends 1GB, so enter 1024MB, choose fat32, and set the mount point to /boot.

Swap space does not have to equal RAM; if hibernation is required, plan around the actual image size and reliable resume testing. Swap relates to virtual memory and hibernation. Choose either a swap partition or a swapfile: the former is simpler to configure, while the latter is slightly more complex but more flexible. Swap partition: create a disk partition the same size as RAM and choose the swap type. Swapfile: allocate all remaining space to one partition, choose btrfs, enable compress (transparent compression, which can save disk space), and add subvolumes.
@swap maps to /swap. For creating the swapfile, see Swap - ArchWiki
Choose grub for bootloader: mainstream distributions use it, configuration is straightforward, and there are many online posts to consult when troubleshooting.
Create a Regular User and Grant Administrator Privileges
profile can preinstall a desktop environment; choose one if needed. After selecting a desktop, you can also select a graphics driver to install.
Choose the kernel for your hardware and workload; validate power consumption, responsiveness, and driver compatibility for both linux and linux-zen.
For network configuration, choose the third option, networkmanager, because mainstream desktop environments integrate with it by default.
Under additional packages, select vim and os-prober; for the zen kernel, also select linux-zen-headers.
